questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes Current Awareness Services (CAS) from Selective Dissemination of Information (SDI)?

options.A: CAS distributes new material according to each user's individual profile, while SDI alerts everyone in a subject area.
options.B: CAS keeps users informed about newly available information in a subject area, while SDI distributes new material according to each user's individual interests or profile.
options.C: CAS and SDI are two different names for the same abstracting service.
options.D: CAS supplies only full-text documents, while SDI supplies only citations without abstracts.

questions.explanation: CAS keeps users informed about newly available information within a subject area of interest, whereas SDI distributes newly available material according to the individual interests or profile of each user.

questions.stem: How do abstracts help the users of a bibliographic database?

options.A: They replace the assigned indexing terms in the database record.
options.B: They let a user judge the relevance of a document before deciding whether to obtain the full text.
options.C: They guarantee that the full text of every record is available online.
options.D: They arrange the records in the database alphabetically by author.

questions.explanation: The abstract helps a user judge the relevance of a document before deciding whether to obtain the full text, and it lets a user screen hundreds of search results efficiently.

questions.stem: Which group consists only of major indexing and abstracting services discussed in this chapter?

options.B: Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning and text mining
options.C: Scopus, Web of Science and PubMed/MEDLINE
options.D: Current Awareness Services, Selective Dissemination of Information and automated summarisation

questions.explanation: Scopus, Web of Science and PubMed/MEDLINE are named as well-known indexing and abstracting services; CINDEX, Sky Index and Macrex are indexing software packages, not services.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes extractive summarisation from abstractive summarisation?

options.A: Extractive methods generate newly worded text, while abstractive methods lift sentences from the original document.
options.B: Extractive methods select important words, phrases, or whole sentences directly from the source document, while abstractive methods represent the meaning using newly generated wording.
options.C: Extractive methods are used only by AI systems, while abstractive methods are used only by human abstractors.
options.D: Extractive methods always distort the original meaning, while abstractive methods never omit important details.

questions.explanation: Extractive methods work by selecting text that already existed in the original; abstractive methods attempt to represent the meaning using newly generated wording.

questions.stem: Why should AI-generated abstracts always be checked against the original source?

options.A: Because AI systems cannot process very large collections of material quickly.
options.B: Because their output may sometimes omit important details or distort the original meaning.
options.C: Because AI-generated abstracts are always produced by extractive methods only.
options.D: Because checking is required before an abstract can be added to any bibliographic record.

questions.explanation: Modern AI systems can assist with abstractive summarisation, but their output may omit important details or distort the original meaning, so it always requires careful checking against the source.
